{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kotohira Shrine (金刀比羅神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = File:金刀比羅神社神門と灯籠.jpg | location = {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|en|Kyoto Prefecture|WD=Q120730|lt=Kyoto}}, [[Kyotango City|Kyotango]], [[Mineyama Town|Mineyama]], Izumi 1165-2 | coordinates = {{Coord|35.62094444|N|135.06116667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | Deities = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大物主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}} | Classification = Former [[Prefectural Shrine]] | Established = [[1811]] ({{ill|Culture|en|Culture|WD=Q11042|lt=Bunka}} 8) | MainHall = {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|en|Nagare-zukuri|WD=Q210684|lt=Nagare-zukuri}} | Alternatename = Tango no Konpira-san | AnnualFestival = October 10 | Rituals = Spring, Summer, Autumn Konpira Festivals | location = {{ill|Kyotango|WD=Q513897}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|WD=Q10936701}} }}
'''Kotohira Shrine''' (金刀比羅神社) is a {{ill|Shinto|en|Shinto|WD=Q812767|lt=Shinto}} shrine located in {{ill|Kyōtango|en|Kyōtango|WD=Q513897|lt=Kyotango City}}, Mineyama Town, Kyoto Prefecture. It was founded in 1811 (Bunka 8) by {{ill|Kyōgoku Takatoshi|ja|京極高備|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyōgoku Takatoshi|1=Kyōgoku Takamasa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11374451}}, the seventh lord of {{ill|Mineyama Domain (Tango)|en|Mineyama Domain (Tango)|WD=Q1073012|lt=Mineyama Domain}}. The shrine is renowned for blessings related to family safety, business prosperity, traffic safety, good luck, safe childbirth, academic success, recovery from illness, and maritime safety. Locally, it is affectionately called "Tango no Konpira-san."<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.konpirasan.com|title=Kotohira Shrine|publisher=Kotohira Shrine|accessdate=2022-10-23}}</ref>
In 2017 (Heisei 29), it was recognized by the {{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|Agency for Cultural Affairs|WD=Q1009519|lt=Agency for Cultural Affairs}} as part of the Japanese Heritage story "Tango Chirimen Corridor," showcasing its historical and cultural significance.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/nihon_isan/pdf/nihon_isan_pamphlet_2019.pdf|title=Japan Heritage Stories|work=Agency for Cultural Affairs|accessdate=2020-11-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story043/index.html|title=Tango Chirimen Corridor|publisher=Japan Heritage Portal|accessdate=2020-11-11}}</ref>
== Deities == ; Main deity * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大物主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}} Known for governing all things, he is revered as the god of abundant harvests, industrial prosperity, epidemic prevention, sake brewing, maritime safety, and national protection. Other names include Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, Yachihoko-no-Kami, and Ōkunidama-no-Kami. He is also the deity of the {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine}}, the primary shrine of Yamato Province.<ref name="#1">Kotohira Shrine Bicentennial Memorial Book</ref>
== History == [[File:金刀比羅神社境内絵図.jpg|thumb|270px|Kotohira Shrine precinct map before the Kita-Tango Earthquake]] [[File:大正期の金刀比羅神社参道正面.jpg|thumb|270px|Kotohira Shrine approach during the Taishō era]] [[File:大正期の金刀比羅神社拝殿と回廊.jpg|thumb|270px|Kotohira Shrine hall and corridors during the Taishō era]]
The shrine was established in 1811 (Bunka 8) under the orders of Kyōgoku Takatoshi, who sought divine favor from {{ill|Kotohira-gū|en|Kotohira-gū|WD=Q94760|lt=Kotohira-gū}} in {{ill|Sanuki Province|en|Sanuki Province|WD=Q929682|lt=Sanuki Province}}. The shrine’s god was enshrined at the request of Takatoshi's family ties to the {{ill|Tadotsu Domain|ja|多度津藩|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tadotsu Domain|1=Tadotsu Domain|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109356835}}, with its construction completed in February 1811.
In 1927, the {{ill|1927 North Tango earthquake|en|1927 North Tango earthquake|WD=Q11400894|lt=Kita-Tango Earthquake}} destroyed the original buildings. Reconstruction began in 1929, and the shrine was restored in 1933.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Kotohira Shrine Bicentennial Memorial Book|publisher=Kotohira Shrine Bicentennial Festival Committee|year=2012|page=4}}</ref>
; Kita-Tango Earthquake The earthquake caused significant damage, including the collapse of the shrine buildings. Rebuilding required substantial funds, much of which came from local donations. A memorial for contributors can be found near the stairs.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Mineyama Historical Records|publisher=Rinsen Shoten|year=1964}}</ref>
; Association with Chōfuku Temple The nearby Chōfuku Temple, under the same Buddhist school, helped facilitate the shrine’s establishment through ties with Konpira’s priests.
== Festivals == The shrine hosts several annual festivals, including: * Spring Grand Festival (April 10) * Summer Grand Festival (July 10) * Water Month Festival and Purification Ceremony (July 29) * Autumn Festival and Portable Shrine Procession (October 10)
== Related People == * Takatoshi Kyōgoku: The founder of the shrine. * Kumagusu Minakata: Documented the shrine’s history and its survival during the Meiji-era Shinto-Buddhist separation.
== Access == * {{ill|Kyoto Tango Railway|ja|京都丹後鉄道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Tango Railway|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to WILLER TRAINS|1=Willer Trains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q19727758}}: 15 minutes on foot from Mineyama Station. * Bus stop: Kotohira Shrine Mae * By car: 20 minutes from {{ill|Yosa Amanohashidate IC|ja|与謝天橋立インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yosa Amanohashidate IC|1=Yoza-Amanohashidate interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11361933}} on the {{ill|Kyoto Jūkan Expressway|en|Kyoto Jūkan Expressway|WD=Q11375668|lt=Kyoto Jūkan Expressway}}.
== External Links == * [http://www.konpirasan.com Official Website]

'''Kotohira Shrine''' (金刀比羅神社) is a {{ill|Shinto|en|Shinto|WD=Q812767|lt=Shinto|1=Shinto}} shrine located in {{ill|Kyōtango|en|Kyōtango|WD=Q513897|lt=Kyotango City|1=Kyōtango}}, Mineyama Town, Kyoto Prefecture. It was founded in 1811 (Bunka 8) by {{ill|Kyōgoku Takatoshi|ja|京極高備|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyōgoku Takatoshi|1=Kyōgoku Takamasa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11374451}}, the seventh lord of {{ill|Mineyama Domain (Tango)|en|Mineyama Domain (Tango)|WD=Q1073012|lt=Mineyama Domain|1=Mineyama Domain (Tango)}}. The shrine is renowned for blessings related to family safety, business prosperity, traffic safety, good luck, safe childbirth, academic success, recovery from illness, and maritime safety. Locally, it is affectionately called "Tango no Konpira-san."<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.konpirasan.com|title=Kotohira Shrine|publisher=Kotohira Shrine|accessdate=2022-10-23}}</ref>
In 2017 (Heisei 29), it was recognized by the {{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|Agency for Cultural Affairs|WD=Q1009519|lt=Agency for Cultural Affairs|1=Agency for Cultural Affairs}} as part of the Japanese Heritage story "Tango Chirimen Corridor," showcasing its historical and cultural significance.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/nihon_isan/pdf/nihon_isan_pamphlet_2019.pdf|title=Japan Heritage Stories|work=Agency for Cultural Affairs|accessdate=2020-11-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story043/index.html|title=Tango Chirimen Corridor|publisher=Japan Heritage Portal|accessdate=2020-11-11}}</ref>
== Deities == ; Main deity * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大物主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}} Known for governing all things, he is revered as the god of abundant harvests, industrial prosperity, epidemic prevention, sake brewing, maritime safety, and national protection. Other names include Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, Yachihoko-no-Kami, and Ōkunidama-no-Kami. He is also the deity of the {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}}, the primary shrine of Yamato Province.<ref name="#1">Kotohira Shrine Bicentennial Memorial Book</ref>

The shrine was established in 1811 (Bunka 8) under the orders of Kyōgoku Takatoshi, who sought divine favor from {{ill|Kotohira-gū|en|Kotohira-gū|WD=Q94760|lt=Kotohira-gū|1=Kotohira-gū}} in {{ill|Sanuki Province|en|Sanuki Province|WD=Q929682|lt=Sanuki Province|1=Sanuki Province}}. In 1927, the {{ill|1927 North Tango earthquake|en|1927 North Tango earthquake|WD=Q11400894|lt=Kita-Tango Earthquake|1=1927 North Tango earthquake}} destroyed the original buildings. Reconstruction began in 1929, and the shrine was restored in 1933.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Kotohira Shrine Bicentennial Memorial Book|publisher=Kotohira Shrine Bicentennial Festival Committee|year=2012|page=4}}</ref>
; Kita-Tango Earthquake The earthquake caused significant damage, including the collapse of the shrine buildings. Rebuilding required substantial funds, much of which came from local donations. A memorial for contributors can be found near the stairs.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Mineyama Historical Records|publisher=Rinsen Shoten|year=1964}}</ref>
; Association with Chōfuku Temple The nearby Chōfuku Temple, under the same Buddhist school, helped facilitate the shrine’s establishment through ties with Konpira’s priests.

{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kotohira Shrine (金刀比羅神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = File:金刀比羅神社神門と灯籠.jpg | location = {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|en|Kyoto Prefecture|WD=Q120730|lt=Kyoto|1=Kyoto Prefecture}}, [[Kyotango City|Kyotango]], [[Mineyama Town|Mineyama]], Izumi 1165-2 | coordinates = {{Coord|35.62094444|N|135.06116667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | Deities = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大物主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}} | Classification = Former [[Prefectural Shrine]] | Established = [[1811]] ({{ill|Culture|en|Culture|WD=Q11042|lt=Bunka|1=Culture}} 8) | MainHall = {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|en|Nagare-zukuri|WD=Q210684|lt=Nagare-zukuri|1=Nagare-zukuri}} | Alternatename = Tango no Konpira-san | AnnualFestival = October 10 | Rituals = Spring, Summer, Autumn Konpira Festivals | location = {{ill|Kyotango|WD=Q513897|1=Kyōtango}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|WD=Q10936701|1=Ōmononushi}} }}
'''Kotohira Shrine''' (金刀比羅神社) is a {{ill|Shinto|en|Shinto|WD=Q812767|lt=Shinto|1=Shinto}} shrine located in {{ill|Kyōtango|en|Kyōtango|WD=Q513897|lt=Kyotango City|1=Kyōtango}}, Mineyama Town, Kyoto Prefecture. It was founded in 1811 (Bunka 8) by {{ill|Kyōgoku Takatoshi|ja|京極高備|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyōgoku Takatoshi|1=Kyōgoku Takamasa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11374451}}, the seventh lord of {{ill|Mineyama Domain (Tango)|en|Mineyama Domain (Tango)|WD=Q1073012|lt=Mineyama Domain|1=Mineyama Domain (Tango)}}. The shrine is renowned for blessings related to family safety, business prosperity, traffic safety, good luck, safe childbirth, academic success, recovery from illness, and maritime safety. Locally, it is affectionately called "Tango no Konpira-san."<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.konpirasan.com|title=Kotohira Shrine|publisher=Kotohira Shrine|accessdate=2022-10-23}}</ref>
In 2017 (Heisei 29), it was recognized by the {{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|Agency for Cultural Affairs|WD=Q1009519|lt=Agency for Cultural Affairs|1=Agency for Cultural Affairs}} as part of the Japanese Heritage story "Tango Chirimen Corridor," showcasing its historical and cultural significance.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/nihon_isan/pdf/nihon_isan_pamphlet_2019.pdf|title=Japan Heritage Stories|work=Agency for Cultural Affairs|accessdate=2020-11-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story043/index.html|title=Tango Chirimen Corridor|publisher=Japan Heritage Portal|accessdate=2020-11-11}}</ref>
== Deities == ; Main deity * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大物主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}} Known for governing all things, he is revered as the god of abundant harvests, industrial prosperity, epidemic prevention, sake brewing, maritime safety, and national protection. Other names include Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, Yachihoko-no-Kami, and Ōkunidama-no-Kami. He is also the deity of the {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}}, the primary shrine of Yamato Province.<ref name="#1">Kotohira Shrine Bicentennial Memorial Book</ref>
== History == [[File:金刀比羅神社境内絵図.jpg|thumb|270px|Kotohira Shrine precinct map before the Kita-Tango Earthquake]] [[File:大正期の金刀比羅神社参道正面.jpg|thumb|270px|Kotohira Shrine approach during the Taishō era]] [[File:大正期の金刀比羅神社拝殿と回廊.jpg|thumb|270px|Kotohira Shrine hall and corridors during the Taishō era]]
The shrine was established in 1811 (Bunka 8) under the orders of Kyōgoku Takatoshi, who sought divine favor from {{ill|Kotohira-gū|en|Kotohira-gū|WD=Q94760|lt=Kotohira-gū|1=Kotohira-gū}} in {{ill|Sanuki Province|en|Sanuki Province|WD=Q929682|lt=Sanuki Province|1=Sanuki Province}}. The shrine’s god was enshrined at the request of Takatoshi's family ties to the {{ill|Tadotsu Domain|ja|多度津藩|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tadotsu Domain|1=Q109356835|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109356835}}, with its construction completed in February 1811.
In 1927, the {{ill|1927 North Tango earthquake|en|1927 North Tango earthquake|WD=Q11400894|lt=Kita-Tango Earthquake|1=1927 North Tango earthquake}} destroyed the original buildings. Reconstruction began in 1929, and the shrine was restored in 1933.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Kotohira Shrine Bicentennial Memorial Book|publisher=Kotohira Shrine Bicentennial Festival Committee|year=2012|page=4}}</ref>
; Kita-Tango Earthquake The earthquake caused significant damage, including the collapse of the shrine buildings. Rebuilding required substantial funds, much of which came from local donations. A memorial for contributors can be found near the stairs.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Mineyama Historical Records|publisher=Rinsen Shoten|year=1964}}</ref>
; Association with Chōfuku Temple The nearby Chōfuku Temple, under the same Buddhist school, helped facilitate the shrine’s establishment through ties with Konpira’s priests.
== Festivals == The shrine hosts several annual festivals, including: * Spring Grand Festival (April 10) * Summer Grand Festival (July 10) * Water Month Festival and Purification Ceremony (July 29) * Autumn Festival and Portable Shrine Procession (October 10)
== Related People == * Takatoshi Kyōgoku: The founder of the shrine. * Kumagusu Minakata: Documented the shrine’s history and its survival during the Meiji-era Shinto-Buddhist separation.
== Access == * {{ill|Kyoto Tango Railway|ja|京都丹後鉄道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Tango Railway|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to WILLER TRAINS|1=Kyoto Tango Railway|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q19727758}}: 15 minutes on foot from Mineyama Station. * Bus stop: Kotohira Shrine Mae * By car: 20 minutes from {{ill|Yosa Amanohashidate IC|ja|与謝天橋立インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yosa Amanohashidate IC|1=Yoza-Amanohashidate interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11361933}} on the {{ill|Kyoto Jūkan Expressway|en|Kyoto Jūkan Expressway|WD=Q11375668|lt=Kyoto Jūkan Expressway|1=Kyoto Jūkan Expressway}}.

He is also the deity of the {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}}, the primary shrine of Yamato Province.<ref name="#1">Kotohira Shrine Bicentennial Memorial Book</ref>
== History == [[File:金刀比羅神社境内絵図.jpg|thumb|270px|Kotohira Shrine precinct map before the Kita-Tango Earthquake]] [[File:大正期の金刀比羅神社参道正面.jpg|thumb|270px|Kotohira Shrine approach during the Taishō era]] [[File:大正期の金刀比羅神社拝殿と回廊.jpg|thumb|270px|Kotohira Shrine hall and corridors during the Taishō era]]
The shrine was established in 1811 (Bunka 8) under the orders of Kyōgoku Takatoshi, who sought divine favor from {{ill|Kotohira-gū|en|Kotohira-gū|WD=Q94760|lt=Kotohira-gū|1=Kotohira-gū}} in {{ill|Sanuki Province|en|Sanuki Province|WD=Q929682|lt=Sanuki Province|1=Sanuki Province}}. The shrine’s god was enshrined at the request of Takatoshi's family ties to the {{ill|Tadotsu Domain|ja|多度津藩|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tadotsu Domain|1=Q109356835|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109356835}}, with its construction completed in February 1811.
In 1927, the {{ill|1927 North Tango earthquake|en|1927 North Tango earthquake|WD=Q11400894|lt=Kita-Tango Earthquake|1=1927 North Tango earthquake}} destroyed the original buildings. Reconstruction began in 1929, and the shrine was restored in 1933.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Kotohira Shrine Bicentennial Memorial Book|publisher=Kotohira Shrine Bicentennial Festival Committee|year=2012|page=4}}</ref>
; Kita-Tango Earthquake The earthquake caused significant damage, including the collapse of the shrine buildings. Rebuilding required substantial funds, much of which came from local donations. A memorial for contributors can be found near the stairs.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Mineyama Historical Records|publisher=Rinsen Shoten|year=1964}}</ref>
; Association with Chōfuku Temple The nearby Chōfuku Temple, under the same Buddhist school, helped facilitate the shrine’s establishment through ties with Konpira’s priests.
== Festivals == The shrine hosts several annual festivals, including: * Spring Grand Festival (April 10) * Summer Grand Festival (July 10) * Water Month Festival and Purification Ceremony (July 29) * Autumn Festival and Portable Shrine Procession (October 10)
== Related People == * Takatoshi Kyōgoku: The founder of the shrine. * Kumagusu Minakata: Documented the shrine’s history and its survival during the Meiji-era Shinto-Buddhist separation.

金刀比羅神社 (京丹後市)
{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kotohira Shrine (金刀比羅神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = File:金刀比羅神社神門と灯籠.jpg | location = {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|en|Kyoto Prefecture|qid=Q120730|lt=Kyoto|1=Kyoto Prefecture}}, [[Kyotango City|Kyotango]], [[Mineyama Town|Mineyama]], Izumi 1165-2 | coordinates = {{Coord|35.62094444|N|135.06116667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | Deities = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大物主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}} | Classification = Former [[Prefectural Shrine]] | Established = [[1811]] ({{ill|Culture|en|Culture|qid=Q11042|lt=Bunka|1=Culture}} 8) | MainHall = {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|en|Nagare-zukuri|qid=Q210684|lt=Nagare-zukuri|1=Nagare-zukuri}} | Alternatename = Tango no Konpira-san | AnnualFestival = October 10 | Rituals = Spring, Summer, Autumn Konpira Festivals | location = {{ill|Kyotango|qid=Q513897|1=Kyōtango}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|qid=Q10936701|1=Ōmononushi}} }}
'''Kotohira Shrine''' (金刀比羅神社) is a {{ill|Shinto|en|Shinto|qid=Q812767|lt=Shinto|1=Shinto}} shrine located in {{ill|Kyōtango|en|Kyōtango|qid=Q513897|lt=Kyotango City|1=Kyōtango}}, Mineyama Town, Kyoto Prefecture. It was founded in 1811 (Bunka 8) by {{ill|Kyōgoku Takatoshi|ja|京極高備|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyōgoku Takatoshi|1=Kyōgoku Takamasa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11374451}}, the seventh lord of {{ill|Mineyama Domain (Tango)|en|Mineyama Domain (Tango)|qid=Q1073012|lt=Mineyama Domain|1=Mineyama Domain (Tango)}}. The shrine is renowned for blessings related to family safety, business prosperity, traffic safety, good luck, safe childbirth, academic success, recovery from illness, and maritime safety. Locally, it is affectionately called "Tango no Konpira-san."<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.konpirasan.com|title=Kotohira Shrine|publisher=Kotohira Shrine|accessdate=2022-10-23}}</ref>
In 2017 (Heisei 29), it was recognized by the {{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|Agency for Cultural Affairs|qid=Q1009519|lt=Agency for Cultural Affairs|1=Agency for Cultural Affairs}} as part of the Japanese Heritage story "Tango Chirimen Corridor," showcasing its historical and cultural significance.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/nihon_isan/pdf/nihon_isan_pamphlet_2019.pdf|title=Japan Heritage Stories|work=Agency for Cultural Affairs|accessdate=2020-11-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story043/index.html|title=Tango Chirimen Corridor|publisher=Japan Heritage Portal|accessdate=2020-11-11}}</ref>
== Deities == ; Main deity * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大物主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}} Known for governing all things, he is revered as the god of abundant harvests, industrial prosperity, epidemic prevention, sake brewing, maritime safety, and national protection. Other names include Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, Yachihoko-no-Kami, and Ōkunidama-no-Kami. He is also the deity of the {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|qid=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}}, the primary shrine of Yamato Province.<ref name="#1">Kotohira Shrine Bicentennial Memorial Book</ref>
== History == [[File:金刀比羅神社境内絵図.jpg|thumb|270px|Kotohira Shrine precinct map before the Kita-Tango Earthquake]] [[File:大正期の金刀比羅神社参道正面.jpg|thumb|270px|Kotohira Shrine approach during the Taishō era]] [[File:大正期の金刀比羅神社拝殿と回廊.jpg|thumb|270px|Kotohira Shrine hall and corridors during the Taishō era]]
The shrine was established in 1811 (Bunka 8) under the orders of Kyōgoku Takatoshi, who sought divine favor from {{ill|Kotohira-gū|en|Kotohira-gū|qid=Q94760|lt=Kotohira-gū|1=Kotohira-gū}} in {{ill|Sanuki Province|en|Sanuki Province|qid=Q929682|lt=Sanuki Province|1=Sanuki Province}}. The shrine’s god was enshrined at the request of Takatoshi's family ties to the {{ill|Tadotsu Domain|ja|多度津藩|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tadotsu Domain|1=Q109356835|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q109356835}}, with its construction completed in February 1811.
In 1927, the {{ill|1927 North Tango earthquake|en|1927 North Tango earthquake|qid=Q11400894|lt=Kita-Tango Earthquake|1=1927 North Tango earthquake}} destroyed the original buildings. Reconstruction began in 1929, and the shrine was restored in 1933.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Kotohira Shrine Bicentennial Memorial Book|publisher=Kotohira Shrine Bicentennial Festival Committee|year=2012|page=4}}</ref>
; Kita-Tango Earthquake The earthquake caused significant damage, including the collapse of the shrine buildings. Rebuilding required substantial funds, much of which came from local donations. A memorial for contributors can be found near the stairs.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Mineyama Historical Records|publisher=Rinsen Shoten|year=1964}}</ref>
; Association with Chōfuku Temple The nearby Chōfuku Temple, under the same Buddhist school, helped facilitate the shrine’s establishment through ties with Konpira’s priests.
== Festivals == The shrine hosts several annual festivals, including: * Spring Grand Festival (April 10) * Summer Grand Festival (July 10) * Water Month Festival and Purification Ceremony (July 29) * Autumn Festival and Portable Shrine Procession (October 10)
== Related People == * Takatoshi Kyōgoku: The founder of the shrine. * Kumagusu Minakata: Documented the shrine’s history and its survival during the Meiji-era Shinto-Buddhist separation.
== Access == * {{ill|Kyoto Tango Railway|ja|京都丹後鉄道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Tango Railway|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to WILLER TRAINS|1=Kyoto Tango Railway|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q19727758}}: 15 minutes on foot from Mineyama Station. * Bus stop: Kotohira Shrine Mae * By car: 20 minutes from {{ill|Yosa Amanohashidate IC|ja|与謝天橋立インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yosa Amanohashidate IC|1=Yoza-Amanohashidate interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11361933}} on the {{ill|Kyoto Jūkan Expressway|en|Kyoto Jūkan Expressway|qid=Q11375668|lt=Kyoto Jūkan Expressway|1=Kyoto Jūkan Expressway}}.
